question: Does the better V25 recipe survive an empty-format control with the same auxiliary loss coefficient?
motivation: V25 selector1.0 native143/255 beat historical direct0.1 at127, but its own direct138 and clean empty139 explain most of the point gain. The historical direct auxiliary coefficient differs.

treatment.auxiliary_target: Empty Evidence field only; no support IDs or factual notes.

comparisons.selector1: Completed original V25 terminal256, same auxiliary1.0.
comparisons.direct0_1: Completed original V23 direct terminal256; isolates the format-weight change.

fixed: Same source documents, order, exposures, view schedule, final-answer serialization, source/final weights, optimizer, LR, precision, topology and loss normalization.
No new packing, forward, backward, batching, ordering or checkpoint function. Only validation/identity/recovery-release guards change.
Auxiliary label counts differ by design: empty-format8192 versus selected-field39930 labels over four passes. Equal coefficients are not equal gradient magnitudes or information.

source.CPU_checks: 1823 passed in62.90s; smoke and compile pass.

numerical_equivalence.limit: Only new validation/identity/qualification guards change. New control still needs actual hardware qualification.

primary.endpoint: Completed selector1.0 direct-answer canonical EM minus new format1.0 direct-answer EM on unchanged held255.
primary.criterion: At least3 percentage points and positive paired95% lower bound identifies promising conditional developmental evidence, not confirmation.
primary.uncertainty: 20000 paired question bootstrap draws, lexicographic item IDs, seed2026101926+contrast_index; no pooling repeated modes or tokens.
primary.interpretation: The cohort motivated these changes and is already inspected. Report point/interval even if the criterion fails; a failed criterion is not proof of zero effect.

secondary: Selector1.0 native own minus format1.0 direct: practical recipe comparison.
Selector1.0 canonical-empty minus format1.0 canonical-empty, identical closed-field/answer-prefill interface.
New format1.0 direct minus historical format0.1 direct.
Same ordinary256 NLL cost versus B0/selector1.0/historical controls; paired pages,20000 draws, seed2026101926+100+index.
Canonical token F1/attributed aliases, unsupported/caps/errors, any regenerated ID/header diagnostics, actual actions and reserved chip-time.

evaluation.parser: Existing anchored Final parser for native direct; bare first-answer-line parser after canonical answer prefill.
evaluation.no_new_oracle: Existing V25 own/empty/oracle readouts remain unchanged. No new teacher or support filter.
evaluation.numerical_kernel: Reuse W2 decoder and W4 ordinary scorer; current-model CPU references and own-model native/cache/calibration checks are still mandatory.

decision: If coefficient matching removes the apparent advantage, do not promote a content-specific claim or tune more coefficients.
If an advantage persists, any capability/internalization claim needs a separately frozen, larger fresh confirmation; no automatic campaign.
This control cannot change the existing inconclusive V25 same-model extra-ID contrasts or failed V25 fitting gate.

stages: Fresh-process restore4 then updates5-8 with full6/8
qualification.audit: All four actual full states2/4/6/8; masks/counts/order/master/moment/cast bytes and restored4 optimizer digests;16 native checks repeat4 canonical contexts.

storage.relocation: Two inactive engineering EBS model duplicates get cross-volume verified replacement copies; original full states retained. Receipt must complete before release.

authorization: This design is preparation, not a learning-run release. Separate bounded qualification release requires source/storage review; science requires its actual passing audit.
limits: Single order seed,TRAIN2048,previously inspected held255; no general-reasoning,pretraining-novelty or calibration claim.
Imperfect support annotations remain unchanged; every model sees all20 passages.
No dataset/model-size/RL/stack/cloud changes or official DEV/TEST access.
